Answer one navigation question about the F# repo at /home/user/yession (~440 .fs files). Read-only: do not edit or write files, do not build, run tests or run `check`, do not use git. Be quick; stop once confident. Always give rg a path (`rg PATTERN .`); without one it can hang reading stdin.

Tools: rg/grep, Grep, Glob and Read, PLUS a warm F# language server (fsautocomplete, compiler-accurate, each call < 1s), called through Bash:
  /tmp/lspq/b3-01-R2-LSP definition <file> <line> <symbol-or-column>
  /tmp/lspq/b3-01-R2-LSP references <file> <line> <symbol-or-column>   (all uses of that exact symbol, workspace-wide)
  /tmp/lspq/b3-01-R2-LSP hover <file> <line> <symbol-or-column>        (inferred type/signature)
  /tmp/lspq/b3-01-R2-LSP symbols <name>                                (find declarations by name)
Files repo-relative, line and column 1-based; a symbol name finds its first whole-word match on the line, so pass a column when the name occurs twice. Use whichever tools you judge best.
The repo's AGENTS.md rule "Finding F# symbols", verbatim:
"""
Never search for a bare name. F# reuses one identifier for a type, its module, a union case and
record fields. Search for the declaration form, then scope to the owning file:

```
rg '^\s*(type|module|let|and)\s+Foo\b'
```

Each `.fsproj` lists `<Compile Include>` in order, and a symbol is declared in its file or an
earlier one. Text search cannot find an inferred type. Follow the right-hand side to its
declaration, or write the type you expect and let `check` tell you.
"""
